transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because… I keep having thoughts that my wife and the kids would be better off if I didn’t wake up. Lately I’ve been saying I don’t need to see another winter, and that scared them enough to get me in here.
How long have you been having these thoughts about your family being better off without you?
It started after my bowling partner died… that was about a year and a month ago. Since then, those thoughts have been there.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed most of the time since your bowling partner died?
I’m not sure I can say “most of the time.” I haven’t really kept track of it like that. I just know things haven’t felt right since he died.
Have you been enjoying the things you used to enjoy, like bowling, since your partner died?

No… not really. I used to look forward to things—bridge, working in the garden, helping with the cooking at church, even going to Cubs games. Now I mostly just sit in my chair, and I can’t make myself care about any of it.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or look forward to?
Not really. I used to look forward to bridge, working in the garden, cooking at church, going to Cubs games… but now I mostly just sit in my chair. I can’t seem to make myself care about any of it.
Have you thought about how you would end your life if you decided to go through with it?

I haven’t really worked out a way to do it, no. It’s more that I keep thinking my wife and the kids would be better off if I just didn’t wake up. Lately I’ve been saying I don’t need to see another winter.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been keeping track of my weight lately.
Do you feel like you're moving more slowly than usual or having trouble sitting still?

Yes… slower. My wife says I move like I’m walking through deep snow. Even getting dressed takes me forever, and just crossing the kitchen feels like too much sometimes. I start to do something and then I just… give up before I get much done.
Do you often feel guilty about things?
Yes. All the time, really. I keep going back over every little thing I did wrong with him… and with my family. I feel like I’m no good to anybody, and like I deserve whatever punishment is coming.
Are you able to experience pleasure when good things happen to you or when something positive occurs?

Not really, no. I used to look forward to things—playing bridge, working in the garden, helping with the church cooking, even going to Cubs games. Now I mostly just sit in my chair, and I can’t seem to make myself care about any of it.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that aren't really there?

Yes… I have. Some evenings I hear his voice, clear as anything, coming from the hallway or the spare room. He says I should’ve been there, or that I failed him. My wife tells me the house is quiet, but I hear it.
How long have you been feeling this way, with no pleasure in activities and thoughts about your family being better off without you, continuously?
It’s been pretty much continuous since my bowling partner died… about a year and a month ago. I haven’t really felt right since then.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or having an inability to sit still?

Not so much fidgeting. It’s more the opposite. My wife says I move like I’m walking through deep snow. Even getting dressed or just crossing the kitchen takes me so long, I end up giving up before I’ve done much of anything.
Have you had any periods of a few weeks or more where you felt better and didn't have these thoughts about your family being better off without you since your bowling partner died?
No… I don’t think so. It’s been going on since he died, about a year and a month now. I haven’t really had a stretch of weeks where it lifted.
Are you able to feel happy or excited when something good happens to you?

Not really. Things I used to look forward to—bridge, working in the garden, cooking at church, even going to Cubs games—I just… I can’t make myself care about them anymore. Mostly I just sit in my chair.
Are you able to enjoy or find pleasure in anything at all anymore?
No… not really. I used to enjoy bridge, working in the garden, cooking at church, going to Cubs games. Now I mostly just sit in my chair, and I can’t make myself care about any of it.
Are there any small things that still bring you a little bit of joy or pleasure?

No… I can’t really think of anything. I used to look forward to bridge, working in the garden, cooking at church, going to Cubs games… little things like that. Now I mostly just sit in my chair, and I can’t make myself care about any of it.
Have you had two or more years where you felt depressed or had a loss of interest in things most of the time?
No, not two years. It’s been since my bowling partner died… about a year and a month ago. Since then I’ve felt this way most of the time.
Have you ever felt depressed or had a loss of interest in things for two years or more at any point in your life?
No, I don’t think so. Not for two years or more. This has been going on since my bowling partner died… about a year and a month ago.
Have you ever had a period in your life before your bowling partner died when you felt depressed or had a loss of interest in things for at least two weeks?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I had bad days like anyone, but I don’t remember anything like this, where it went on for weeks and I lost interest in things.
